# A sharp retained-mass corollary with a true integer-base centroid

Let C be a convex body in R^n x R^d with nonempty mixed intersection S,
intrinsic dimension q>=1, intrinsic measure mu=H_q|S, and total mass M.
For EVERY continuous normal u nonconstant on each positive q-dimensional
fiber direction space, there exists ONE actual ambient closed halfspace H
such that

    mu(H)=M/2^n,

and the TRUE unweighted intrinsic centroid of `C intersect H intersect
Lambda` has integer base. The retained intersection is induced by a full
ambient convex body, and its centroid belongs to it. The fraction 2^-n
cannot be improved uniformly. This is a retained-mass theorem; no sharp
continuous depth bound is asserted at this mixed centroid.

## 1. A weighted Doignon center in the base

Let P be the positive q-volume integer bases, with masses w_z, and put
`m=2^n`, `t=M/m`. There is an integer j such that every closed base
halfspace containing j has marginal mass at least t.

Here is the standard finite weighted Doignon argument, including the strict
threshold. For every subset A of P with `sum_(z in A)w_z>M-t`, take conv A.
Any at most m such sets have a common point of P: their complements have
total weight strictly less than `m t=M`, by the union bound. Doignon's
integer Helly theorem therefore gives an integer point j common to all
these finitely many convex hulls. Including A=P puts j in conv P. If a
closed halfspace containing j had marginal mass less than t, its strict
complement in P would have mass greater than M-t. Its convex hull lies
strictly outside that closed halfspace, a contradiction. For n=0 the
unique base point gives the assertion directly, with m=1.

This argument uses closed halfspaces for depth and strict complements for
the contradiction; boundary fibers are not discarded.

## 2. Membership in the mass-t moment body

Consider the compact convex set

    Z_t={sum_z s_z z:0<=s_z<=w_z, sum_z s_z=t}.

For every vector a, the marginal depth statement supplies at least t
weight on indices with `a.z>=a.j`. Allocate exactly t dominated mass
among those indices, using fractional allocation if needed. It follows
that

    h_(Z_t)(a)>=t a.j.

Finite-dimensional separation now gives `t j in Z_t`. Thus the exact
mass/base-moment target `(t,tj)` belongs to the zonotope of feasible
source moments. No hypothesis that j is the original marginal mean has
been used.

## 3. One actual convex cap and its centroid

Apply `candidate 46f947c28385c3ea` to the target
`(t,tj)` and the prescribed generic continuous normal u. It produces one
finite actual cap H with exactly that mass and moment. Since t>0, the
intersection `D=C intersect H` is a full ambient convex body and its
mixed intrinsic dimension is q. Its true intrinsic centroid has base j
and belongs to D by compact convexity. It is therefore an actual point
of `D intersect Lambda`, not a rounded point or a weighted surrogate.

The same integer j obtained in Section 1 works for every admissible u;
the cap offset and integer tilt may depend on u. The generic directions
exist because q>=1 and only finitely many positive fiber direction spaces
must be avoided.

## 4. Sharpness and the counting boundary

Take any q-dimensional convex body K in R^q, with q>=1, and the full case
`d=q`,

    C=[0,1]^n x K.

Its 2^n positive fibers all have volume v=|K| and M=2^n v. If ANY positive
dominated submeasure has integer base centroid, that centroid lies in
the binary cube and is a binary vertex j. For each coordinate, a mean
of zero or one of a [0,1]-valued source forces that coordinate to equal
its mean almost everywhere. Hence the entire retained mass lies on the
single base j and is at most v=M/2^n. This applies in particular to every
convex cap-subbody or arbitrary convex subbody. Therefore the universal
retained fraction is sharp even in the full mixed-dimensional class.

For q=0, Sections 1--2 still give a feasible fractional source moment,
but Section 3 is false in general: an actual counting cap cannot realize
noninteger mass. For instance the three integer points of C=[0,2] have
M=3,n=1, so the requested exact mass M/2 is 3/2. The counting centerpoint
bound has its own direct Doignon proof and is not inferred through this
continuous cap-realization theorem.

The theorem does not prove OC. A mixed source with an integer-base true
centroid need not have continuous Grünbaum depth gamma_d, and a retained
centroid's depth in the original source cannot be assigned that constant
without an additional proved argument.
